criterion_notes.c1: No. The study examines end-user preferences and microbiological disinfection efficacy across five household point-of-use (POU) water treatment technologies (boiling, SODIS, WaterGuard dilute bleach, PUR flocculant-disinfectant sachets, and silver-coated clay filters) applied to water already collected from existing taps, tanks, rivers, and ponds. Per Exclusion Criterion 3 and the scope discipline rules, household water-quality disinfection product selection without analysis of water supply or sanitation service access does not satisfy Criterion 1.
criterion_notes.c2: No under both readings. Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, although the abstract frames participatory decision-making as a general principle of development governance and one workshop per village included five Village Water Committee members alongside researchers to recommend a donor-subsidized POU product, the study does not examine any legal, administrative, institutional, or regulatory factor governing water service; at best it touches researcher-facilitated stakeholder consultation only tangentially, and the overall plain-wording decision remains exclude because c1 and c4 also fail. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it clearly fails: a 3.5-hour researcher-facilitated Structured Decision Making (SDM) workshop demonstrating donor-supplied POU disinfection methods (with cost explicitly excluded because a private donor subsidized the chosen product) is participatory project delivery and behavioural/technology-choice decision support, not a rule-type mechanism governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure rules, tariffs or cost-recovery, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure).
criterion_notes.c3: Yes. The study presents primary empirical data from six 3.5-hour Structured Decision Making workshops across two rural Tanzanian villages (Milola and Naitolia; 30 participants total across four women's groups and two Village Water Committee groups) combined with field microbiological water-quality assays (IDEXX Colilert-18 tests in replicates of three for E. coli and total coliforms pre- and post-treatment).
criterion_notes.c4: No. Reported outcomes are participants' 0-5 ratings and ordinal rankings of POU disinfection methods on sensory and usability attributes (taste, odor, color, treatment time, ease of use, volume treated per unit time, and perceived health risk), Village Water Committee workshop product recommendations, and pre-/post-treatment presence or absence of E. coli and coliforms. Product cost was explicitly excluded from the tradeoff evaluation, and no household or community outcome measuring water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion is reported.
criterion_notes.c5: Yes. Population and sample (30 workshop participants—two groups of 5 women and one group of 5 Village Water Committee members in each of Milola and Naitolia, Tanzania—plus primary and secondary source water samples), exposure/intervention (3.5-hour Structured Decision Making workshops and demonstrations of five POU disinfection methods), outcomes (attribute consequence matrices, POU rankings/recommendations, and E. coli/coliform assay results), and study design (participatory multi-criteria SDM field workshop case study with pre/post microbiological testing) are all clearly reported.
criterion_notes.c6: Yes. Full text is written in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: To this end, the research reported here focused on the development of a deliberative risk management framework for involving affected stakeholders in decisions about POU water treatment systems.
Following the discussion of objectives, the workshops moved into 60-minute interactive demonstrations of each of the POU methods
The cost of each POU system was also excluded in this analysis
Enough untreated water from each source was drawn for pretreatment testing. The remaining water was divided and treated using each of the available POU systems.
When the scoring of samples across all of the objectives was completed, the results across all of the participants were summarized in a consequence matrix.

raw_response.exposure: 3.5-hour researcher-facilitated Structured Decision Making (SDM) workshops with interactive demonstrations comparing five household point-of-use (POU) water disinfection methods (boiling, SODIS, WaterGuard sodium hypochlorite, PUR flocculant-disinfectant sachets, and silver-coated ceramic clay filters)
raw_response.outcome: Participants' 0-5 attribute ratings and rankings of POU water disinfection methods (taste, odor, color, time, ease of use, volume per unit time, perceived risk), Village Water Committee workshop recommendation of a preferred POU method (WaterGuard), and pre-/post-treatment E. coli and coliform presence/absence assays
raw_response.population_and_sample: 30 rural residents across two villages in Tanzania (Milola in Lindi region and Naitolia in Monduli District): in each village, two workshops of 5 women each (n=10) and one workshop of 5 Village Water Committee members (n=5), plus untreated and POU-treated water samples from local taps, tanks, rivers, and ponds (assayed in triplicate)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (E01 - Wrong topic; also fails c2 and c4). This empirical decision-sciences and water-quality study tests a 3.5-hour Structured Decision Making (SDM) workshop protocol to elicit sensory and usability preferences across five household point-of-use (POU) water disinfection products (and tests their E. coli/coliform removal) in two rural Tanzanian villages. It does not examine water supply or sanitation service access (c1=no), examines participatory donor-project technology demonstrations rather than any legal, administrative, regulatory, or rule-type governance mechanism (c2=no under both narrow rule-type and plain readings, with cost explicitly excluded due to donor subsidy), and reports only sensory/usability ratings, workshop product recommendations, and microbiological disinfection efficacy rather than any service access, connection, availability, continuity, affordability, or exclusion outcome (c4=no).
raw_response.study_design: Participatory multi-criteria Structured Decision Making (SDM) field workshop study combined with pre/post microbiological water-quality testing
